speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this dry cough going on for about two months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but I do notice I get short of breath when I try to move around and there's a whistling sound when I breathe. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That whistling sound suggests wheezing, which points toward an airway issue rather than a heart problem. Since we cannot perform labs or an ECG, can you tell me if you have a history of asthma, allergies, or if you smoke?

speaker: Patient
text: I've been smoking for quite a while, about 20 pack-years, but I don't have any history of asthma or allergies. I also work as a mechanic, so I'm around dust and fumes all day. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and exposure to dust and fumes, along with the dry cough and wheezing, do you experience chest tightness or a sensation of pressure in your chest? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your ankles or legs, or any changes in your urine output?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't feel any tightness or pressure in my chest, but I have definitely noticed some mild swelling in my ankles over the last week. My urine output seems normal, and I haven't had any fever or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with Cor Pulmonale (Right Heart Failure). The combination of long-term smoking, occupational dust exposure, chronic cough, wheezing, and new-onset ankle swelling strongly suggests COPD leading to pulmonary hypertension and right-sided heart failure. The absence of chest pressure and normal urine output further supports a primary respiratory etiology rather than left-sided heart failure.
